record.notes:
AI Malaysia Berhad was itself created the same day from the National AI Office. The 2026-2030 National AI Action Plan does not mention the institute; it calls instead for a national 'AI Trust Function' to evaluate, monitor and respond to AI risks. In September 2026 AI Malaysia's chair still described setting up the institute as a priority in the works. This is the weakest 'established' record in the dataset: designation and mandate are stated in a primary government release, but no head, staff, budget or launch is published.

The ministry identifies AI Malaysia Berhad as a national AI entity under the Ministry of Digital and assigns it the national AI Safety Institute role. The institute's separate legal form and host classification are not specified in this announcement.

head.notes: Searched 19 Oct 2026 (en, ms): MY-AISafe page on ai.gov.my, the MY-AISafe overview PDF, the AI Malaysia home page and news list, the 11 Sep 2026 inaugural board statement (names the AI Malaysia board only: chair Aireen Omar; no MY-AISafe head and no AI Malaysia chief executive), the 28 Jul 2026 launch release (EN on digital.gov.my, MS PDF), the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (E12 AI Trust Function: only a recruitment plan for a "specialised multidisciplinary team"). No named director or head of MY-AISafe in any of them. The contact route is a generic AI Malaysia mailbox.

national_partners.notes: Cyber agency searched: NACSA (National Cyber Security Agency, under the National Security Council, Prime Minister's Department); CyberSecurity Malaysia as second, 2026-10-19 (en, ms); none found. No NACSA, CyberSecurity Malaysia or MyCERT link to MY-AISafe in any fetched document. Searched: MY-AISafe page and overview PDF, AI Malaysia home page, launch release (EN and MS), board statement, National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (full text grep for NACSA, cyber, CERT: NACSA appears only in the abbreviations list, never in the text; the E12 row speaks generically of integrating "cybersecurity, communications, financial and law enforcement agencies" into a coordinated response framework), nacsa.gov.my Act 854 page (Cyber Security Act 2024, in force 26 Aug 2024; contact block: National Security Council, Prime Minister's Department; no AI wording). Not published, not absence of any link. CyberSecurity Malaysia corporate overview and events pages were fetched on 20 October 2026; neither named cooperation with MY-AISafe. The institute overview and action plan also named no such cooperation.

testing_capacity.notes: The institute's overview, marked for reference only, uses the present tense ('MY-AISafe tests systems before release, then manages incidents and tracks emerging threats once they are in use'), but it describes a body launched on 28 July 2026 that was still in preparation in September 2026; this is read as its mandate, not as reported testing. The plan's E12 items sit under its proposed actions, which the overview says the institute delivers. No joint network testing credited to Malaysia was found.

model_access.notes: No access event, legal power or agreement providing for access to, or evaluation of, the models of a developer that has a model in Epoch AI's frontier set was found. The AI Governance Bill was in public consultation from 10 to 31 July 2026, with tabling in Parliament targeted for 2027.

staffing_model.notes: The adopted National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (revision of 18 August 2026) provides under the AI Trust Function (E12) to 'Recruit and train a specialised multidisciplinary team, including AI risk analysts, adversarial machine learning engineers and incident response leads', and AI Malaysia's overview says MY-AISafe delivers that function. No source yet states staff of its own, a host body's staff or posts (searched: the AI Malaysia site and careers page, Ministry of Digital releases, the Budget 2027 speech and Dewan Rakyat answers); the overview says 'The institute draws on expertise from government, industry, academia and research institutions'.

claims.text: The Ministry of Digital's launch release assigns it a pillar of work that covers safety evaluations, testing and AI red teaming.
The Ministry of Digital's launch release assigns it governance, safety and regulatory support through the development of standards, risk management and compliance assurance.
The Dewan Rakyat record says the government set it up, through the Ministry of Digital and AI Malaysia Berhad, to study clear mechanisms for regulating the use of AI in organisations across sectors.
The Dewan Rakyat record says it is responsible for AI governance work covering safety benchmarking, risk assessment and incident reporting for corrective action.
AI Malaysia's overview says the institute delivers the national AI Trust Function, which brings together testing of AI models and applications against standards.
The National AI Office's overview says the institute "develops tests, benchmarks and evaluation reports to assess AI systems against key areas of responsible AI".
The National AI Office's overview says MY-AISafe "manages incidents and tracks emerging threats" once systems are in use.
AI Malaysia's national action plan calls for a national AI Trust Function to evaluate, monitor, anticipate and respond to AI risks, and its overview says MY-AISafe delivers that function.
The ministry says the institute will work through strategic collaborations for talent development, expertise sharing and technology transfer at national and international levels.
AI Malaysia says MY-AISafe tests systems before release, then manages incidents and tracks emerging threats during use.
